info.title: rindetuplata API
info.description: Informational yields for Argentine savers: plazo fijo by bank, remunerated wallets, money-market funds and the dollar MEP, compared by real return against inflation. This API is informational only and is not financial advice: it does not recommend any institution, product or investment decision. Every row names its source id, its date of data and its validation flags.

post.description: Emails a one-time login link. A valid email always answers 202 with the same body, whether or not the account exists and even when the email already holds its maximum of unexpired tokens (then nothing is sent). An invalid email is a 400. Each remote address may make rindetuplata.auth.magic-link-per-ip-limit requests per rindetuplata.auth.magic-link-per-ip-window (fixed window, counted in memory by the single API instance, invalid emails included); beyond it the answer is a 429 with a Retry-After header in seconds, no token and no mail, for known and unknown emails alike.

post.summary: Log in with a magic-link token
post.description: Consumes the one-time token of the magic link and starts the session. A successful login rotates the CSRF token and clears the XSRF-TOKEN cookie, so the client must call GET /api/v1/auth/csrf again before its next state-changing request.

get.description: The active API keys of the signed-in user, oldest first: id, label, display prefix, plan and creation date. The key itself is never returned again.

post.description: Creates a key for the signed-in user and returns it once, in the key field: only its SHA-256 and a display prefix are stored, so it cannot be shown again. A user may hold at most 3 active keys (a 400 beyond that). Send the key in the X-Api-Key header of the public read API to get the FREE plan limits (a bucket per key and a daily quota); a key never authenticates an account endpoint. The body is optional: {"name": label of at most 60 characters}.

get.description: Cacheable by validation. The response carries a weak ETag derived from the version of the stored data and the normalized request, and Cache-Control: public, no-cache. Send the ETag back in If-None-Match to get a 304 with no body while the data and the request are the same; a new ingestion run or a curated-rate change produces a new ETag. Entries carry breakEvenMep and the response carries dollarMep. The dollar MEP break-even of the instrument over the requested days. A saver buys dollars at the MEP sell price today and leaves them at the MEP buy price at the end, so the instrument wins when the MEP buy price rises less than devaluation = (1 + nominalReturn) * sell / buy - 1; the spread is part of the answer. Computed from the quote in dollarMep; null (never invented) when no MEP quote is stored.

200.description: The simulation, ineligible or excluded status.

Cache-Control.description: public, no-cache: store, but revalidate with If-None-Match.

ETag.description: Weak entity tag of the data version and the request.

304.description: If-None-Match matched the current ETag; the body is empty.

400.description: A parameter is out of range.

404.description: No ranked instrument carries this id.

get.description: The closed months that have a report, newest first. A month is listed only when it has ended, INDEC has published its inflation and the stored history covers it; until then the list is empty. Each instrument's nominal return is what it delivered over the closed month, from the stored history. Wallets and crypto compound daily at the latest known rate of each calendar day (a day whose latest capture is more than 3 days old disqualifies the instrument); a plazo fijo locks the non-client TNA of its first capture of the month, which must be dated on or before the first business day, as one term over the month's days (TNA * days / 365); a fund is the ratio of its last quote on or before the month end to its last quote on or before the previous month end, each at most 4 days before that end, and the classes of one fund are grouped to the best one. The real return is (1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation) - 1 against the INDEC monthly inflation of the same month.

get.summary: Who beat inflation in a closed month
get.description: Each instrument's nominal return is what it delivered over the closed month, from the stored history. Wallets and crypto compound daily at the latest known rate of each calendar day (a day whose latest capture is more than 3 days old disqualifies the instrument); a plazo fijo locks the non-client TNA of its first capture of the month, which must be dated on or before the first business day, as one term over the month's days (TNA * days / 365); a fund is the ratio of its last quote on or before the month end to its last quote on or before the previous month end, each at most 4 days before that end, and the classes of one fund are grouped to the best one. The real return is (1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation) - 1 against the INDEC monthly inflation of the same month. Rows are sorted by real return, best first; instruments that could not be measured are returned apart with their reason.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: The month as yyyy-MM, for example 2026-10.

400.description: The month is not a valid yyyy-MM.

404.description: The month is not closed yet, INDEC has not published its inflation, or the stored history does not cover it.

get.summary: Banks with today's plazo fijo rates
get.description: Every bank that has a valid plazo fijo snapshot at or before today, sorted by slug, with its latest non-client and client TNA (fractions, scale 6) and the capture and data dates of that snapshot. A rate is null when the bank does not publish it.

get.summary: One bank: rates, 90-day series and best-rate days
get.description: The bank's latest rates, its non-client TNA per capture day over the last 90 calendar days ending today (inclusive, America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires, oldest first) and bestDays/observedDays: among the capture days of that window on which the bank had a valid non-client TNA (observedDays), the days on which it was the highest among all banks (bestDays). A tie counts for each bank tied; invalid snapshots and days the bank was not captured are left out.

The raw CSRF token the SPA sends as the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on every state-changing request; the same response writes the XSRF-TOKEN cookie. The header is compared against the raw value, so this is the token to hand the client, never the masked request attribute. Public: no session is needed to ask for one.

delete.description: Revokes one of the caller's active keys; it stops working on the next request. An unknown id, a key of somebody else and an already revoked key are the same 404.

BreakEvenMepView.description: The dollar MEP break-even of the instrument over the requested days. A saver buys dollars at the MEP sell price today and leaves them at the MEP buy price at the end, so the instrument wins when the MEP buy price rises less than devaluation = (1 + nominalReturn) * sell / buy - 1; the spread is part of the answer. Computed from the quote in dollarMep; null (never invented) when no MEP quote is stored.

devaluation.description: The highest rise of the MEP buy price, as a fraction at scale 6 (0.023100 is 2.31%), at which the instrument still beats the dollar over the requested days.

price.description: The break-even MEP buy price in ARS per USD at scale 2: (1 + nominalReturn) * sell. Above it at the end of the term the dollar wins; below it the instrument wins.

MepQuoteView.description: The dollar MEP quote every breakEvenMep of the response was computed from: the latest stored quote at or before the request's asOf. Null when no usable quote is stored.

buy.description: ARS per USD the market pays for a dollar (the price you leave at), scale 2.

sell.description: ARS per USD the market charges for a dollar (the price you buy at), scale 2.

quoteDate.description: The capture date the quote is stored under.

updatedAt.description: The instant the source reports for the quote; null when it gave none.

ReportCoverageView.description: The days of the month the nominal return was measured over, out of the days of the month. Wallets, crypto and plazo fijo cover the whole month by construction; a fund covers the days from the previous month end to its last quote (at least the month minus 4 days).

value.description: The month's inflation as a fraction (1.9% is 0.019), scale 6.

observationDate.description: The date the observation is stored under: the last day of the month it measures.

reason.description: NOT_CAPTURED_AT_START, GAP_IN_CAPTURES, MISSING_BASE_QUOTE, MISSING_END_QUOTE, NOT_OFFERED_TO_NON_CLIENTS, INVALID_DATA, FOREIGN_CURRENCY, RESTRICTED_CLASS or FUND_CLASS_NOT_FOUND.

nominal.description: The return the instrument delivered over the month, as a fraction (2% is 0.02).

real.description: (1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation) - 1 against the INDEC rate of the month.

beatInflation.description: True when the real return, as published, is above zero.

BankRatesView.description: A bank with the latest valid plazo fijo rates stored at or before today.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier derived from the bank name: lowercase, accents stripped, non-alphanumerics as dashes. Stable; a name collision takes a numeric suffix in instrument id order.

instrumentId.description: Id of the bank's instrument, usable with /api/v1/instruments/{id}/history.

nonClientTna.description: Non-client TNA as a fraction, scale 6; null when the bank offers none.

clientTna.description: Client TNA as a fraction, scale 6; null when the bank publishes none.

captureDate.description: The day the rates were captured.

dataDate.description: The date the source says the rates are about.

BankDetailView.description: A bank's latest plazo fijo rates, its 90-day non-client TNA series and bestDays/observedDays.

instrumentId.description: Id of the bank's instrument, usable with /api/v1/instruments/{id}/history.

nonClientTna.description: Non-client TNA as a fraction, scale 6; null when the bank offers none.

clientTna.description: Client TNA as a fraction, scale 6; null when the bank publishes none.

captureDate.description: The day the latest rates were captured.

dataDate.description: The date the source says the latest rates are about.

series.description: Non-client TNA per capture day inside the window, oldest first.

bestDays.description: Capture days in the window on which this bank's non-client TNA was the highest among banks; a tie counts for every bank tied.

observedDays.description: Capture days in the window on which this bank had a valid non-client TNA: the denominator of bestDays.

BankSeriesPoint.description: A capture day and the bank's non-client TNA (fraction, scale 6) captured that day.
